fixes.explanation: Paul, an apostle writing to the believers in Rome (Romans 1:1, 7), says it plainly: "I consider that our present sufferings are not comparable to the glory that will be revealed in us." (Romans 8:18) Not comparable. These two don't even fit on the same scale, friend. I think that's the kind of math that lets a tired person breathe a little.

I get why angels come to mind. But they're not in this verse at all. Paul says the creation is waiting "…for the revelation of the sons of God." (Romans 8:19) Angels are off the guest list for this one.

The prophets don't come up in this verse, friend. Paul says the creation "…waits in eager expectation for the revelation of the sons of God." (Romans 8:19) It's the sons of God being revealed that creation is watching for. Good guess, but that's a different tray.

Storms never come up in this verse, friend. Paul says the creation "…will be set free from its bondage to decay and brought into the glorious freedom of the children of God." (Romans 8:21) Notice the word bondage. The hope is that creation gets set free from it, and that's a bigger promise than a break from the weather.

Rest sounds wonderful after a long day, but that's not what Paul says here. He says believers "…groan inwardly as we wait eagerly for our adoption as sons, the redemption of our bodies." (Romans 8:23) The groaning is real, and what they're waiting for is the redemption of their bodies. Paul ties the hope right to the body.

A home in the promised land sounds like a place, but this verse doesn't name one. Paul says believers wait for "…our adoption as sons, the redemption of our bodies." (Romans 8:23) He defines adoption right there, friend. It's the redemption of our bodies.

I know that kind of waiting well, the fretting kind. But Paul says, "But if we hope for what we do not yet see, we wait for it patiently." (Romans 8:25) The word is patiently, not nervously. Paul puts hope and patience together.

That's it. Paul says, "…the Spirit Himself intercedes for us with groans too deep for words." (Romans 8:26) That's help for when we don't know how we ought to pray. Those groans go deeper than any sentence we could put together.

True. Paul says, "…the Spirit intercedes for the saints according to the will of God." (Romans 8:27) The Spirit's praying runs along the will of God. That's good news when we don't know how we ought to pray.

That's actually true, friend. Paul says, "…the Spirit intercedes for the saints according to the will of God." (Romans 8:27) The Spirit's praying lines up with God's will. That's good news when we don't know how we ought to pray.

Priests and a holy temple sound weighty, but this verse doesn't mention them. Paul says God predestined those He foreknew "…to be conformed to the image of His Son…" (Romans 8:29) That's the destination here. It's about becoming like the Son.

Angels aren't in this verse. Paul says the Son would be "…the firstborn among many brothers." (Romans 8:29) And look who the brothers are: the ones God predestined "…to be conformed to the image of His Son…" It's a family picture, friend, with the Son as the firstborn.
